posts.text:
Friday, Nov 27: Toronto's streetcars lost 908 hours to delays, across all routes.

Slowest for its length: 509 Harbourfront westbound. A typical 2.6 km trip lost 8 min (usually 7).
Smoothest: 507 Long Branch westbound, 13 min over 8.0 km (usually 12).

#TTC #TransitSky #DataViz

https://stuckin.to/

Friday's slowest spot: Eastbound on Queens Quay West, between Lake Shore Blvd W and Lower Spadina Ave.
The average streetcar lost 2 min 3 s here (usually 71 s). Across 133 trips, that adds up to 4.5 hours.
The biggest share was at the Lower Spadina Ave light, which has transit priority.
posts.alt: 3D map of Queens Quay West around Lower Spadina Ave, rotated to Toronto's street grid. Delay is drawn as a coloured ridge above the track, rising where streetcars lose time; the eastbound stretch between Lake Shore Blvd W and Lower Spadina Ave is highlighted, adding up to about 2 min 3 s lost per streetcar.

posts.text:
Most short-turned, Friday, Nov 27: 501 Queen. 1 in 11 trips (30) were sent back before the end of the line, most after Queen St East at Kingston Rd (eastbound, 13), instead of going on to Neville Park.

Across all routes, 4% of trips were short-turned.
posts.alt: Map of the 501 Queen route in the waits view: a column at each stop, taller and darker where riders waited longer than scheduled, and yellow warning signs where cars were short-turned. A tooltip on the busiest spot, after Queen St East at Kingston Rd, gives how many eastbound cars were sent back there instead of going on to Neville Park.

posts.text:
Most held at a signal, Friday, Nov 27: westbound at Strachan Ave & Fleet St.

1 in 2 streetcars waited 90 s or more beyond a clean approach, about a full signal cycle, despite transit priority.
About 289 streetcars came through.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Strachan Ave & Fleet St, with arrows for each direction of streetcar travel into each signal, coloured by how often streetcars were held 90 seconds or more. A tooltip for the westbound approach reads 50% held 90 s+, with a histogram of extra time through the approach.

posts.text:
Friday, Nov 27: at the busiest moment (6:30 pm), 150 streetcars were in service, against 151 scheduled.
Overall, 99% of scheduled streetcar service ran, and buses ran 1,185 hours on streetcar routes.
Furthest behind: 505 Dundas, at 93% of its scheduled service.
posts.alt: Line chart of streetcars in service through Friday, Nov 27, every 10 minutes from 4 am, against the TTC's schedule (dashed). The busiest moment was 150 streetcars at 6:30 pm, against 151 scheduled; over the day 99% of scheduled streetcar hours ran.

posts.text:
Longest extra wait at a stop, Friday, Nov 27: Bay St at Elm St (506 Carlton westbound).

A car was due about every 10 min, so the average wait should have been about 5. It was 14.7: about triple.

Turn up at random and the chance of waiting over 10 min was 28%. On schedule: under 1%.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Bay St at Elm St in the waits view, a column at each stop. A tooltip for the stop reads a 14.7 minute average wait, 9.8 more than on schedule, with a 28% chance of waiting over 10 minutes against 0% on schedule, and a chart of the spread of gaps between cars.
